seoTitle.en: Heroes of the Glowing Shore: the real animals behind The Littlest Guardian

description.en: The world's smallest penguin, a kiwi that smells with the tip of its beak, and an island of glowing skies. Real, checked facts for kids.

intro.en: Every animal in The Littlest Guardian is real, and they share the beaches of New Zealand. Here is how they eat, grow and find their way home.
The book's beach has no name, so we picked one where little penguins live and kiwi really walk on the sand: Stewart Island / Rakiura, at the bottom of New Zealand.

text.en: Rakiura means "glowing skies", after the southern lights, the aurora australis, that shine over the island.

title.en: A park on most of the island

text.en: Rakiura National Park covers about 85% of the island. There are only 28 km of road but 280 km of walking tracks.
Brown kiwi outnumber people on Stewart Island! Only about 400 people live there.
In 2019 the island became an International Dark Sky Sanctuary, a place protected for its starry nights.
The rainbow shell in the story looks like pāua, a big sea snail found only in New Zealand. Its scientific name means "rainbow ear-shell", and its blood is light blue!
A long wild beach on the west coast of Stewart Island / Rakiura, where scientists have studied tokoeka families for decades.

job.en: The littlest guardian of the path home

value.en: About 25–33 cm, the smallest penguin in the world
About 1 kg, like two blocks of butter
About 7 years on average; the oldest known reached 25
Small fish, squid, octopus and crustaceans
Burrows, rock cracks, under bushes, logs, even under houses
Couples share the eggs and the chicks
At Risk: Declining in New Zealand

text.en: Their scientific name, Eudyptula, means "good little diver". They chase fish underwater, usually in water less than 50 m deep.
Little penguins come ashore only under the cover of darkness. They gather in small groups offshore at dusk, called rafts, and waddle home together, usually with the same friends each night.
Once a year they stay on land for about two weeks to replace all their feathers at once. Until the new coat grows in, they can't swim, so they can't eat!
At their nests they bray, squeal and growl. Colonies are loudest just after dusk.
Little penguins use their paddle-like flippers to 'fly' through the water at up to 6 km/h.
A little penguin can eat about its own body weight in food every day.
They squeeze oil from a gland near the tail and rub it through their feathers to stay waterproof.
Dogs are the biggest threat to little penguins. Cats, ferrets, stoats and cars on coastal roads kill them too. Keeping dogs on a lead near beaches helps.

storyVsReal.en: Real little penguins really do walk the same path home every night, all in a group. But a penguin with baby fluff on its head would still be a chick waiting at the nest, not out on the beach. And penguins don't tidy paths: people do that job for them.

superpower.en: Nostrils on the tip of her beak

value.en: About 45 cm
Males about 2.4 kg, females about 3.1 kg
Expected to live about 26 years
Earthworms, grubs, insects and fallen fruit
Forest, scrub and dunes of Stewart Island/Rakiura
Family groups with big brothers and sisters as helpers
At Risk: Naturally Uncommon; about 13,000–15,000 birds

text.en: Most kiwi only come out at night. Rakiura tokoeka are unusual: they're often active in the daytime too, and some even hunt for food on the beach.

title.en: A beak that smells and feels

text.en: Kiwi are the only birds with nostrils at the tip of the beak. Tiny sensing pits there can feel worms wriggling underground, up to 3 cm deep.
Young Rakiura tokoeka can stay with their family for up to seven years and help sit on Mom and Dad's eggs, up to a fifth of the time.
Kiwi can't see well. They feel their way with cat-like whiskers and find food mostly by smell and touch.
A kiwi egg is about 20% of its mother's weight, and six times bigger than normal for a bird its size. The tokoeka's egg is pale green and about 13 cm long.
To push its beak deep into the soil, a kiwi sometimes kicks its legs up and leans its whole weight on its beak: a kiwi headstand!
Kiwi have wings, only about 3 cm long, hidden in their feathers. Each one has a little claw on the tip.
Tokoeka means "weka with a walking stick" in the Ngāi Tahu dialect, after its long beak.
Tokoeka eggs take 70 to 80 days to hatch, and both parents take turns keeping them warm.

storyVsReal.en: Rakiura tokoeka really do walk on beaches, sometimes in daylight. But real kiwi don't carry shells. Aroha's rainbow shell looks just like a pāua shell, a real New Zealand sea snail.

superpower.en: From egg to sea in about 3 months

value.en: Usually two
30–39 days, kept warm by both parents
18–38 days with a parent on the nest
Food brought up from the parent's tummy
At about 7–8 weeks old
Usually at 2–3 years old

text.en: From about 5 weeks old, chicks wait outside the burrow on their own while both parents fish at sea all day.
Chicks hatch covered in soft down. Their waterproof feathers grow in before their first trip to sea.
In its first year, a young little penguin can travel more than 1,000 km.
Little penguins can doze while floating on the sea.

storyVsReal.en: Real chicks stay hidden near the nest until they're ready for the sea. They wouldn't carry sticks along the path. The white feather on one chick's chest is our artist's idea.

text.en: Pick up three pieces of litter on your next walk, with a grown-up and gloves. Little things add up!
Keep your arms by your sides like flippers and waddle across the room. Can you do it in a line, like a raft of penguins coming home?
Hide something smelly, like an orange peel, under a cup. Can you find it with your nose and eyes closed?
A kiwi egg is about 20% of its mom's weight. Ask a grown-up to work out how heavy an egg that big would be for you!
Find New Zealand on a map, then the little island at the very bottom: Stewart Island / Rakiura.

q.en: Are the animals in The Littlest Guardian real?

a.en: Yes. Little penguins and kiwi both live in New Zealand, and on Stewart Island / Rakiura kiwi even walk on beaches. Each hero file tells you what we changed for the story.

q.en: Do kiwi really go on the beach?

a.en: The Rakiura tokoeka does. It's often active in daytime too, which is rare for a kiwi.

q.en: How can I help little penguins?

a.en: Keep dogs on a lead near beaches, especially around dusk and dawn, drive slowly on coastal roads, and leave burrows alone.

q.en: Why do penguins come ashore at night?

a.en: Coming ashore in the dark helps them avoid some of their natural predators.
